program.name: Medicare Savings Program (MSP)
program.description:
Medicare Savings Program (MSP) helps people with Medicare pay their monthly premiums. If your income is low enough, it may also cover your deductibles, copays, and other out-of-pocket costs.

If approved, MO HealthNet pays your Medicare Part B premium to Medicare for you. You won't get a check. Instead, if that premium is taken out of your Social Security now, it will stop, so your monthly payment goes up. If you pay Medicare by bill, those bills stop. There are three levels of MSP, and the one you qualify for determines how much help you get. At the highest level (QMB), doctors and hospitals also can't charge you deductibles, copays, or coinsurance for care that Medicare covers. Prescriptions work separately: QMB also signs you up for Extra Help, which brings most drug copays down to a few dollars.

MSP has a limit on the assets you can own, but many things don't count. Things that don't count: your home, one vehicle, household goods, burial funds, and life insurance.

Select Apply Online to start your Medicare Savings Program application.

documents.text: Proof of home address (ex: lease, utility bill)
Proof of identity (ex: driver's license, official state ID card)
Social Security Number or proof you applied for one
Medicare card showing Part A enrollment, if you have one. You can also apply with proof that you applied for Part A or that you conditionally enrolled for QMB.
Proof of earned income, if requested (ex: pay stubs, W-2, 1099)
Proof of unearned income, if requested (ex: Social Security, pension statement)
Proof of resources (ex: bank statements, investment accounts). Do not include your home, one vehicle, household goods, or a burial fund
Proof of U.S. citizenship or qualified immigration status

navigators.name: Missouri State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
navigators.description: Missouri SHIP offers free, unbiased Medicare counseling from trained volunteers. They can explain your Medicare options. They help you compare plans. They also assist with billing and enrollment issues. These counselors don’t sell insurance or charge fees. So, you get objective advice across the state.
